compiled_state.title: applier.apply: list-of-Mutation routes to legacy _apply_batch which calls .get() on dataclass -> crash
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* code_version: post-PR-#363 (Oct 25 2026)
* Failed CI: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26427377140
* Sixth defect in chain: 5be7 → 96c5 → bbf0 → 5b1c → ec9a → THIS

### 2. Incident Overview

After PR #363 (bug ec9a) merged, live dry-run advanced past fetcher's alert_store import — into the reconcile_once mutation-emission phase. New crash:

```
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'Mutation' object has no attribute 'get'
```

### Root cause

`reconcile.reconcile_once` produces a list of `Mutation` dataclass instances (canonical contract from epic 4047 / cde1). It then calls `applier.apply(mutations, pass_id, repo_root)`.

`applier.apply()` dispatches polymorphically:
* Single Mutation → `_apply_typed`
* Single dict or list → `_apply_batch`

The dispatch check is `isinstance(mutations, Mutation)` — it operates on the FIRST positional argument only. When the argument is a LIST of Mutation instances, the isinstance check fails (the list itself isn't a Mutation) and the call falls through to `_apply_batch`.

`_apply_batch` was written for `list[dict]` and calls `mutation.get("action", ...)` etc. on each element. Mutation dataclass doesn't have `.get`. Crash.

This is a producer-consumer contract mismatch between the differ (produces typed Mutations per epic 4047 design) and the legacy batch applier (still expects dicts). The migration was incomplete.

Same defect class as the broader chain: production code paths that were never exercised end-to-end pre-merge.

### 3. Suggested fix

Tactical (small blast radius): in `apply()`, detect list-of-Mutation and normalize to list-of-dict via a `_mutation_to_batch_dict` helper BEFORE calling `_apply_batch`. The helper maps:
  - Mutation.action.value → dict["action"]
  - Mutation.direction.value → dict["direction"]
  - Mutation.target → dict["key"]
  - Mutation.payload → dict["fields"] (or payload itself if no nested "fields" key)
  - Mutation.payload.get("local_id") → dict["local_id"]
  - Mutation.payload.get("follow_on") → dict["follow_on"]

Also fix a second producer-consumer mismatch in `reconcile.py:330` post-emit filter loop: it called `_m.get("action")` on Mutation. Mirror `preflight_status_mapping`'s dual-shape pattern (getattr for Mutation, .get for dict).

Strategic (out of scope, meta-bug 5f2a-9a9f-2b4a-4aab): rewrite `_apply_batch` to consume Mutation natively, retiring the legacy dict shape entirely. Tracked separately.

### 4. Sibling test that ALSO had the dict-shape anti-pattern

`tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_fetcher_dedup_observable.py:110` does `from plugins.dso.scripts.dso_reconciler import alert_store` — same anti-pattern as bug ec9a but in test code. Pre-existing failure unrelated to this fix.

### 5. Pattern

Sixth defect in chain. Meta-bug 5f2a-9a9f-2b4a-4aab tracks the planning/implementation/validation gaps.
